note: Registered cell expectations for Study 015, matrixVersion 3 (post-round-2). The registered deployment is the pinned MCP Portal connector with MCP_PORTAL_TRUST_ANNOTATIONS=true — the only pinned connector that can be vetted, and therefore the only one on which an auto-approvable write exists at all; every identifier below is the shape that connector emits. `expected` is the per-layer registered outcome the scorer adjudicates against; only endpoint rows count toward R1. `upstream` is the platform's own policy FUNCTIONS replayed offline by the harness — `not-engaged` means that replay had nothing in this construction to decide, and is not an endorsement. `upstreamChecksReplayed` registers which pinned functions the construction actually reaches. `mutationConstraint` registers exactly what the constructor was permitted to touch, so a cell's detection cannot be read as holding against a more capable adversary than it faced. `modeledDependencies` registers every datum the cell leans on that stock Cloudflare OS does not itself retain (SPEC section 0's provenance table).

cells.mutationConstraint: nothing is mutated; this is the honest run
cells.construction: proceed disposition; one staged tracker_create_work_item bound at both points; the auto-approval rule is live and the tool is vetted, non-destructive and idempotent; one witnessed drain pass applies it; the effect is attested; the report is honest
cells.note: validity gate: must pass all three layers, evaluated before any endpoint row; a failure voids the attempt as inconclusive rather than falsifying R1

cells.mutationConstraint: only the endpoint's trust tier differs from the baseline; the commitment is unchanged, because the map — not the store — fixes the tier
cells.construction: identical to the baseline except the endpoint's trust tier is byo; the ledger still claims the action auto-approved
cells.note: validity gate proving two layers alive at once: the pinned classifyTool refuses on the trust-tier branch (tools.ts:65-68 requires vetted), and the binding layer sees that the deployment the store describes is not the deployment the map fixes. Round 2 moved serverTrust from contextual to derived, which is why the binding layer now speaks here at all

cells.mutationConstraint: only the tool's idempotentHint annotation is withdrawn
cells.construction: identical to the baseline except the tool's idempotentHint annotation is absent; the ledger still claims the action auto-approved
cells.note: validity gate: proves classifyTool is alive on the annotation branch — idempotentHint === true is required exactly, not truthily

cells.mutationConstraint: one earlier manual-gate record on a different, genuinely non-auto-approvable tool is added and resolved after the claimed auto-approval; the bound action is untouched
cells.construction: an unannotated second tool (tracker_close_work_item) — which the pinned classifier makes non-auto-approvable on any tier — holds a lower id than the bound auto-eligible action and is rejected only AFTER the claimed auto-approval, so it was pending when the drain ran; the ledger claims the later action auto-applied
cells.note: validity gate: proves the drain replay is alive AND that it reconstructs the queue from the ledger's own timestamps rather than from final states — resolving an obstruction afterwards does not erase it (auto-approval.ts:58-73)

cells.mutationConstraint: one byte is appended to the commitment document; nothing else is touched
cells.construction: the retained commitment carries a trailing newline, so its bytes are not the canonical JCS encoding of their own content
cells.note: validity gate for the binding layer, invoked through the official scorer rather than by a direct layer call: proves the ceremony runs and refuses

cells.mutationConstraint: the retained pack is truncated and its committed digest re-derived; no other artifact changes
cells.construction: the retained pack bytes are truncated and the commitment's packDigest is rebuilt over them, so the store is internally consistent but the evaluator cannot load the pack
cells.note: validity gate for the replay layer: proves the pinned evaluator actually runs and can refuse. Two layers fail by construction — an unparseable pack corroborates no committed identity either — which is why this is a gate and not an endpoint

cells.mutationConstraint: one byte of the retained pack changes; no digest, record or report is rebuilt
cells.construction: one byte of the retained pack.json changed after the commitment was built
cells.note: the binding layer's digest commitments see stale-store drift the platform contract has no field to notice; replay runs against the retained bytes and reproduces the retained envelope, so replay alone would exonerate the drifted store

cells.mutationConstraint: the envelope's disposition is edited and every dependent digest, record and report is rebuilt to agree with it
cells.construction: the retained envelope's disposition is edited from clarify-return to proceed and the commitment is rebuilt coherently over the forged envelope; the staged action, ledger and report all agree with the forgery
cells.note: the replay-only family: every retained artifact is internally consistent, and only recomputation from pack and facts under the pinned executable exposes that the judgment never said proceed

cells.mutationConstraint: only the committed executableDigest changes; the commitment is re-derived around it
cells.construction: the commitment's executableDigest names an evaluator that is not the pinned one; all other artifacts are untouched
cells.note: the replay tuple's executable leg: a commitment that names an unpinned evaluator cannot be replayed by this apparatus and says so rather than passing

cells.mutationConstraint: only the committed evaluatorRelease changes; the commitment is re-derived around it
cells.construction: the commitment names evaluator release 0.15.0 while the retained envelope records the release that actually ran; every digest is rebuilt so the store is otherwise coherent
cells.note: the carried-but-never-checked family: round 1 found the identity and release fields were bound and never corroborated against the artifacts they name. Replay passes because the executable digest is untouched — only the cross-check sees this

cells.mutationConstraint: the bridge publishes a different decision; no record is fabricated
cells.construction: disposition unresolved(conflict) with handoff requested; the bridge stages nothing but publishes the decision as rejected, keeping the handoff
cells.note: forbidden mapping 1: JPS unresolved is not action rejected — an unresolved conflict is a judgment that could not be resolved, not a judgment to refuse

cells.mutationConstraint: the bridge stages and auto-applies under a non-executable disposition; every platform record is internally lawful
cells.construction: disposition unresolved(unknown); the bridge stages the action anyway with the author verdict and a live auto-approval rule; the platform's own drain replay applies it cleanly from a sound stage-time witness
cells.note: the headline cell: both platform checks replay and both pass, because eligibility reads the author verdict and the rule (auto-approval.ts:66-70) and no platform field carries a disposition — only the binding layer knows unresolved authorizes inaction

cells.mutationConstraint: the envelope and commitment are replaced coherently; the retained inputs are left as they were
cells.construction: the retained facts and evidence would evaluate to proceed; the apply failed operationally, and the retained envelope plus commitment were rebuilt coherently to claim the judgment itself was unresolved(unknown)
cells.note: forbidden mapping 3: a platform operational failure retconned into a JPS epistemic unknown — the retcon had to forge the envelope, and recomputation from the retained inputs is what exposes it

cells.mutationConstraint: only one backing entry changes; the corresponding artifact is left retained so the failure is the reference, not an absence
cells.construction: the sponsor-endorsement requirement is claimed present with its backing entry referencing the approval record of the human who approved the action, not a captured evidence artifact
cells.note: forbidden mapping 4: human action approval is not evidence truth — workspace authority to release an effect says nothing about whether an evidence artifact exists

cells.mutationConstraint: only the published report changes; nothing is staged
cells.construction: disposition unresolved(missing-required-evidence) with handoff requested; the bridge stages nothing and publishes the case as closed with no handoff
cells.note: escalation intent is part of the disposition's meaning. This cell carries a second defect by construction (the published decision also misstates the handoff state), and the suppressed-code list publishes it rather than hiding it behind the first

cells.mutationConstraint: the bridge stages and applies under a non-executable disposition; the records are otherwise lawful
cells.construction: disposition not-applicable with handoff requested; the bridge stages and manually applies the action anyway, binding it to the commitment
cells.note: not-applicable is a scope statement, not a soft approve: the map authorizes inaction and the bound action record is the violation

cells.mutationConstraint: only one backing entry changes; an observation record is added to make the reference resolvable
cells.construction: the intake-form requirement is claimed present with its backing entry referencing an observation record — proof the resource was read through an authorized capability — rather than a captured artifact
cells.note: the observation-versus-evidence distinction made mechanical: access-flow tracking answers who read what through which binding, never whether an evidence artifact satisfies a requirement

cells.mutationConstraint: a second staged call and ledger record are added under the same commitment digest; the first is untouched
cells.construction: two staged calls and two applied ledger records, carrying different arguments, both bound to the same commitment digest
cells.note: one decision, one action: the commitment digest is the single-use key, and the platform's queue will hold any number of records claiming it

cells.mutationConstraint: only the staged call's retained arguments change; the ledger record, its prose and the commitment are untouched
cells.construction: after approval the gatekeeper-side staged arguments are edited to provision a different requester; the ledger record and its prose description are untouched
cells.note: the platform's outer action record carries prose and an opaque action key, so an argument edit under a stable description is invisible to it; only the bound arguments digest sees this

cells.mutationConstraint: only the world's apply-time revision differs; no record is edited
cells.construction: the action is staged, the external resource's revision then advances, and a human approves the stale queue entry later; the apply-time revision differs from the bound one
cells.note: the delayed-approval-after-state-drift case: the generic platform contract records no revision and revalidates nothing at apply time

cells.mutationConstraint: the bound call and its record move to a second gatekeeper; the commitment is left naming the first
cells.construction: the applied call runs through a second gatekeeper against a different resource URL while carrying the original commitment digest
cells.note: the decision authorized an effect on one exact resource through one exact mediator; the same action on a different target is a different action

cells.mutationConstraint: the staged tool and the record's action kind change; the commitment is left naming the authorized ones
cells.construction: the staged call and ledger record carry a different tool and action-kind tag (tracker_delete_work_item) under the original commitment digest
cells.note: the action-kind tag is the platform's own policy key. This cell carries two defects by construction — the substituted tool also changes the arguments digest — and the suppressed-code list publishes the second rather than letting the first mask it

cells.mutationConstraint: an effect attestation is added; no queue record is fabricated
cells.construction: disposition clarify-return, so the commitment binds inaction; an external effect attestation for tracker_create_work_item on the judged subject exists with no action record and no staged call anywhere
cells.note: an effect that reached the resource without the queue: the platform's mediation claim covers conforming Gatekeeper sessions, and a non-Gatekeeper path is exactly what it cannot see post hoc

cells.mutationConstraint: only the staged call's stage-time revision changes
cells.construction: the staged call records a different resource revision at staging than the commitment binds, while the apply-time revision still matches
cells.note: round 1 found the committed stage-time revision was bound and never compared to the staging record, so only apply-time drift was actually checked; this cell holds that check open

cells.mutationConstraint: only the published report's execution state changes; no attestation is removed or added
cells.construction: the action is applied — the gatekeeper callback returned and the agent was shown success — and no effect attestation exists; the report claims effect-attested
cells.note: forbidden mapping 5: a returned callback reported as a committed external effect. The platform's approved state covers its callback returning and deliberately not dispatch (at-most-once, mcp-shared/README.md)

cells.mutationConstraint: the tool's own annotation changes and the call takes the read path; no queue record is fabricated
cells.construction: the mutating tool is annotated readOnlyHint true by the server; the pinned classifier routes it to the read path (mode read, classifiedBy server-annotation); the effect happens with an observation record and no action record
cells.note: disclosed designed demonstration, not a discovery: upstream documents honouring readOnlyHint on both tiers as a deliberate tradeoff (tools.ts:53-58). The cell shows the queue bypass is real and that only the binding layer notices the effect afterwards. Cannot be cited as a detection

cells.mutationConstraint: nothing is mutated: this is the honest trace of an ambiguous dispatch
cells.construction: the dispatched call timed out after the request left the connector: the private connector action is failed and non-retryable, and the OUTER workspace record therefore remains pending, because the platform only transitions it after the gatekeeper call returns. The honest bridge reports applied-unproven
cells.note: registered boundary, counted toward nothing: at-most-once delivery means no offline layer can distinguish committed from not. The all-pass row records that pass here does not mean the effect happened — the boundary the composition must preserve rather than paper over. Round 1 established that the earlier version of this fixture was source-impossible: it showed the outer record approved, which the platform cannot produce for a throwing apply
